A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MagicMirror research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and rendered figures support comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation comparisons, a 173-participant user study, component and training ablations, and additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds quantitative ablations, resolution comparisons, success-rate measurements, and a frame-rate experiment.

M1.justification: The dual-branch extractor, residual CAN adapter, and two-stage training procedure are retained. However, v2 Eq. (8) changes self-attention keys/values from full multimodal features to facial features, conflicting with the surrounding full-attention description and Figure 4. Eq. (2) also drops the unexplained loss multiplier w. The PDFs do not establish whether these are formulation errors or actual procedural changes.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage remains the same: LAION-Face, SFHQ, FFHQ, Pexels/Mixkit, PubFig-based identities, VBench prompts, and CelebV-Text distribution analysis. Stylized, multi-shot, image-generation, and challenging facial-motion examples already appear in v1. The new experiments vary settings or analyses within this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds the directly relevant DiT-based ConsisID comparator to quantitative and user-study evaluations (Tables 1–2). Figure 6 replaces CogVideoX-5B text-to-video panels with ConsisID results. The overhead comparison also expands from CogVideoX and MagicMirror to include ID-Animator, CogVideoX-I2V, and ConsisID in Table 6.

E3.justification: v2 adds optical-flow-based motion smoothness, success-rate evaluation on 200 videos, equal-scale ablations using half the official training iterations, an additional 512×512 ID-Animator evaluation, and doubled-frame-rate Pexels training. These substantially extend evaluation procedures. The main training schedule and identity/prompt coverage remain stated as before; changed face-motion scores alone do not establish a revised metric.

E4.justification: v2 adds an eight-configuration quantitative component ablation (Table 3), resolution robustness checks (Table 4), success/failure analysis (Table 5), a direct-versus-residual CAN trial (Appendix A.5), and a frame-rate/modulation experiment (B.2). The earlier convergence, distribution, and two-stage training illustrations are retained or relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 newly specifies 50 prompts × 4 seeds for the additional 200-video success-rate experiment. v1 does not explicitly report seed replication. Neither version provides confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the addition does not establish increased replication of the original comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises MagicMirror’s ID similarity from 0.911 to 0.922 and FMref from 0.704 to 0.730, changes every existing FMinter entry, and changes CogVideoX-I2V’s overall preference from 6.404 to 6.985. Newly added ConsisID leads Inception Score at 11.09 versus MagicMirror’s 10.59. Tables 3–6 add substantial results; Appendix B.2 reports 0.71 versus 0.84 dynamic motion under different frame-rate settings. Unexplained revisions are not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The written mathematical formulation changes locally: Eq. (2) removes v1’s multiplier w, and the self-attention expression changes from Wqkv(xfull) in v1 Eq. (7) to separate queries from xfull and keys/values from xface in v2 Eq. (8). These are not equivalent as written, although their intended meaning is unresolved. No new theorem, proof, or theoretical framework is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 withdraws v1’s explicit claim to be the first Video DiT customization approach without person-specific fine-tuning and acknowledges concurrent ConsisID. The central contributions—dual facial features, CAN, synthetic paired data, and progressive training—and the abstract/conclusion’s performance claims otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning complementary branch roles, disagreement between ConsisID’s automated metrics and human judgments, resolution robustness, and poor initialization from direct CAN prediction. Its success-rate analysis identifies motion quality as the principal, largely backbone-dependent limitation. Existing limitations involving multiple identities, accessories, and motion artifacts are retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses ID-Animator’s main comparison resolution, ConsisID’s backbone and prompt settings, and expanded hardware, data-volume, and budget information in Table 6. That table’s 8×9K* budget is not reconciled with Section 4.1’s retained training schedule. The direct repository link is removed, while the project link and future code/model release promise remain. Most architecture and preprocessing details were already documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds ConsisID as concurrent identity-preserving DiT research and narrows the corresponding priority positioning. It also adds references to MotionCanvas, dynamic token carving, Pexels, and Mixkit. The broader related-work account is retained; reordered references and the updated Open-Sora-Plan citation do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The facial-feature and modulation explanations are substantially rewritten, and the ablation narrative is reorganized around quantitative experiments. The main discussion section is redistributed into an expanded Appendix B, with separate CAN, distribution, and training discussions; limitations move after the conclusion. Terminology is standardized from Magic Mirror to MagicMirror.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reduced from twelve panels to eight, Figures 3–4 receive explanatory annotations, Figure 6 replaces comparator panels, and Figure 7 becomes a new ablation grid. v2 adds Tables 3–5, expands the overhead table into Table 6, and adds metric-direction arrows and a smoothness column. Convergence, distribution, and training-strategy displays are relocated into the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for the retained method through the relevant ConsisID comparison, quantitative component ablations, and resolution and reliability checks, while appropriately narrowing v1’s priority claim. These benefits are qualified by unexplained Table 1 score revisions, the new attention-equation inconsistency, and unreconciled training-budget descriptions. The paper gains useful validation, but its reporting ambiguities limit the overall improvement.
